blocks.title: Rule of the day (2 min)
blocks.text:
a / an = one thing, not known yet. a plan, an invoice.
the = a thing we both know. I sent an email. The email was short.
No article for languages, days and months: English, Monday, November.
After did / does not, use the base verb: He did not take the bus. She does not know.
In a positive past sentence, use the past form: She took the bus. (not: She did take)
Irregular past: take - took, come - came, pay - paid, tell - told.

s_a15_retry.label: Retry: does / did not + base verb

e01.name: Verb after did / does not
e01.note: Negatives and questions in the past got better on Nov 3. On Nov 4 'does not Worked' still appeared.
e01.right: does not work · did not go
e01.rule: After did, did not, does not and Did you...?, the verb stays in the base form. The -ed goes only on did.

e02.name: did in a positive sentence
e02.rule: In a positive past sentence, use the past verb with no did.
e02.wrong: did write · did take · did come

e03.name: he / she + -s in the present
e03.note: On Nov 4: sends and shows were right.
e03.right: He sends · He does not send
e03.rule: Positive: verb + -s. With does or does not, the verb goes back to the base form, with no -s.

e04.name: Articles a / an / the
e04.note: Also seen in 'a Claude plan' and 'the Saturday'.
e04.rule: A singular countable noun almost always needs a, an or the.

e05.name: Word class
e05.note: Your work vocabulary is already good. The problem is the form of the word.
e05.right: I build automations · supplier accounts · reconciled
e05.rule: Nouns, verbs and adjectives have different forms: analysis / analyze, account / accounting.
e05.wrong: I make automation · supply accounts · reconciliate

e06.name: need to + verb
e06.right: I need to check the supplier account
e06.rule: After need comes to + the base verb.

e07.name: Capital letters and apostrophes
e07.note: Some of this may be fast typing.
e07.rule: Days, months and names start with a capital letter. The apostrophe replaces the o in not.

e08.name: Sentence without a verb
e08.note: On Nov 4 answers are still short, but the content is right.
e08.right: Some employees were worried that the meetings would move to other days.
e08.rule: Every answer is a sentence with a subject and a verb.

e09.name: Prepositions with days and places
e09.note: Mistakes with to/for, in/on and at on Oct 31.
e09.rule: on + day (on Saturday), in + month or year (in March), at + time (at 8 pm). to and for change the meaning.

e_doesnt_base.name: Base verb after does not
e_doesnt_base.right: He does not work on Sunday.
e_doesnt_base.rule: After does / doesn't / did / didn't, the main verb stays in the base form.
e_doesnt_base.note: You did it right with "didn't go". Same rule for the present.

e_missing_verb.name: Missing main verb
e_missing_verb.right: She does not know the answer.
e_missing_verb.rule: does not is only the helper. You still need the main verb (know).

e10.name: Irregular past forms
e10.rule: Learn the irregular past: pay - paid, take - took, come - came.

e11.name: Spelling and typos
e11.rule: Check each word once before you send. Use the Translator if you are not sure.

e12.name: Word choice
e12.rule: Some words go together. Learn the pair: build automations, do your best.

e13.name: Verb forms
e13.rule: One sentence, one main verb. Do not put is and went together.

wmw4caqxjeq4.example: The farmer uses hoes in the garden.
wmw4caqxjeq4.note: Remember that regular verbs in English add -ed for past tense, e.g., filed.

wmw4co9bwwlk.example: My hometown is near the office.
wmw4co9bwwlk.note: Remember that nouns like "hometown" are singular; add "s" for plural (hometowns).

wmw4cy5uq698.example: We have tasty meals in the break room.
wmw4cy5uq698.note: Remember that adjectives like "tasty" come before the noun in English, but after the noun in Portuguese (e.g., "refeições saborosas").

wmw4d80lp3x5.note: "Pretty" is an adjective meaning "very" or "quite"; use it before adjectives (e.g., pretty good).

wmw4d8n774r8.example: I am currently reviewing the invoices.
wmw4d8n774r8.note: Use "currently" before the verb to show something happening now.

wmw4dz491t58.example: The manager warned us about greed in the office.
wmw4dz491t58.note: Remember that nouns like "greed" do not change in plural; add an "s" for the plural form (greeds) only when needed.

wmw4e3r5brqf.example: I told my boss the report is ready.
wmw4e3r5brqf.note: "told" is the past tense of "tell"; use it for actions that happened in the past.

m01.why: Pay is irregular: pay - paid. Do not add -ed.

m02.wrong: I don't went to the office.

m02.why: Use did not + base verb for the past negative.

m03.why: In a positive past sentence, use the past form (took). Use "did" only in questions and negatives.

m04.why: Positive past sentence: came, not did come.

m05.why: Positive past sentence: paid, not did pay.

m06.why: The fixed phrase is "do my best".

m07.why: You need the verb am. Check the spelling: excited.

m09.why: The apostrophe replaces the o in did not: didn't.

m11.why: Short adjective or adverb + er: hard - harder.

m12.why: Languages start with a capital letter.

m13.wrong: I was tired, But I worked.
m13.right: I was tired, but I worked.
m13.why: After a comma, "but" has a small b.

m15.why: Use a before a singular noun: a plan.

m16.why: Short form of did not: didn't.

m17.why: Short form of does not: doesn't.

m18.why: Days of the week start with a capital letter.

m19.why: Do not use does and a verb with -s together. Use one: He sends.

m20.why: In English the word is person.

m21.wrong: He does not Worked on Saturday.
m21.right: He does not work on Saturday.
m21.why: After does not, use the base verb: work.

m22.right: I need to check the supplier account.
m22.why: Use need to + verb. Add the article the.

m23.why: Is and went do not go together. Use one verb: went.

m26.why: The English verb is reconcile. Past: reconciled.

m27.why: Say customer advances (money received in advance).
